comparator.name: Economie en Bedrijfseconomie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum totals 180 ECTS. Year 1 is a 60-ECTS common foundation in economics, business, finance, accounting, data and digital skills. In year 2 students take 36 ECTS of common courses and 24 ECTS in either Bedrijfseconomie or Economie. The generic target does not name a specialisation, so the first-listed Bedrijfseconomie route is instantiated by neutral official-order tie-break. Year 3 contains a 30-ECTS mobility/minor/internship window, ethics, a route-specific compulsory course, a 6-ECTS elective and a 12-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit GROW activity is excluded and genuine choice space remains open.
components: Choice among exchange, a 24-ECTS internship plus a 6-ECTS elective, Economics and Management minors, or another Tilburg minor.
Compulsory third-year course for the selected Bedrijfseconomie specialisation.
One course chosen from the six-course published elective list.

alternatives.label: Economics, business & data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response combining micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, strategy, organisations, marketing, statistics, data, AI and research methods.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, mathematical and strategic foundations precede the advanced policy, organisational, international-business, machine-learning, econometrics, behavioural-economics, market-research and finance work. Strategy follows Business Foundations; Probability & Statistics follows Mathematical Methods; Money, Banking & Finance follows business, accounting and economic study. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.
traceOverrides: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods that strengthen empirical economic and business research

alternatives.label: Public economics, institutions & inequality
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum makes public economics, political institutions, law, inequality and policy research its organising emphasis while retaining economics and quantitative foundations.
alternatives.concept: An economics-and-public-policy direction combining markets, macroeconomics and data with political institutions, law, inequality, labour, governance, sustainability and policy research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces accounting, marketing, business strategy, international business, product design, machine learning, probability and finance with comparative politics, sociology, qualitative methods, political philosophy, human rights, constitutional law, sustainability governance, EU politics, social theory, persuasive communication, peace and conflict, and historical research. The resulting curriculum is organised around institutions and policy rather than firms and business functions.
progression: Foundational economics, politics and sociology precede advanced public economics, governance, constitutional law, EU politics, social theory, policy communication and research. Qualitative Research Methodology precedes the final research seminar; Research Methods & Statistics precedes econometrics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Finance, risk & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
alternatives.concept: A financial-economics direction combining investment, money, banking and corporate finance with economic theory, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the generic Economie en Bedrijfseconomie bachelor and does not privilege either year-two specialisation. Bedrijfseconomie is the first specialisation in the official curriculum table, so it is selected before comparison with UCR and independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest curriculum combines economics, business and data around the selected Bedrijfseconomie route. Public economics/institutions and financial economics/risk each support coherent, mechanically feasible and substantially distinct additional programmes. Three alternatives are included, the maximum.

Both examine strategic behaviour, information, uncertainty and microeconomic choice.
Both develop macroeconomic and international-economic analysis; UCR is more advanced and international.
Both analyse taxation and public-sector economic choices; UCR is broader than fiscal economics.
Both introduce firms, markets, strategy and organisational decision-making.
Both develop financial-accounting foundations; UCR also covers corporate finance.
Both address investment, financial markets, risk and financial decision-making; UCR also covers money and banking.
Both examine marketing, consumer engagement and market-facing decisions.
Both examine corporate governance and institutional responsibilities; UCR adds international-business breadth and is not a company-law course.
UCR finance is represented elsewhere and is not duplicated as a second direct match.
UCR has accounting and finance but no dedicated management-accounting course.
UCR has broad business foundations but no dedicated business-administration course in these schedules.
Both provide mathematical foundations for economic and quantitative analysis; UCR is broader.
Both provide research design, statistics and empirical-analysis foundations.
Both introduce data handling, visualisation and analytical reasoning.
Both develop data analysis and predictive modelling; UCR focuses machine learning.
Both introduce programming for analytical problem-solving; UCR uses Python rather than R.
Both develop structured data management for organisational analysis; UCR focuses relational databases and SQL.
UCR develops digital collaboration across courses but has no separate three-ECTS equivalent.
UCR develops data and communication skills across courses but has no separate three-ECTS integration course.
Both examine organisational decisions under sustainability constraints; UCR focuses governance rather than financial management.
Both support reflective competence and professional development; UCR is broader personal and professional development.
Both develop ethical and philosophical analysis; Tilburg focuses science and free markets.
The comparator’s genuine mobility, internship or minor space is not populated with assumed courses.
UCR Ethics is already aligned to the year-two philosophy component and is not duplicated as a second direct match.
The comparator’s six-course elective choice remains open rather than assumed.
UCR optional independent research is shown separately and does not make the Tilburg thesis a direct course match.

notes.text: Tilburg requires a sustained combined economics-and-business sequence, a 24-ECTS specialisation, dedicated accounting and finance courses, and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can create coherent economics, policy and finance pathways but does not reproduce the complete specialist Bedrijfseconomie sequence.
